title: Pack two uneven bearings up to the datum, then seat the beam level across them
instruction: Pack each grey pier with the wooden packers (yellow 20 mm, blue 30 mm, green 40 mm thick) until its top is level with the top of the red-capped datum post behind it, every packer lying flat and fully on the pier. Then lay the beam across both packed piers.
context: Carpenters, structural iron and steel workers and millwrights (O*NET 47-2031, 47-2221, 49-9044) bring each bearing up to the set level, the datum, with packers or shims laid flat and fully on the bearing before a beam, lintel or machine base is set down. The member's level comes from the packing, never from forcing it: a member laid across bad packing sits out of level and bears on one corner, which is the defect. Here the two piers differ in height, so each needs its own packing (the left a two-packer stack), read from the packers' colour code against the datum posts, and the beam goes on only once both are at the datum.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Four kinds of thing are on the table. (1) Piers: two fixed grey concrete blocks standing on the table, each 60 x 60 mm with sides parallel to x and y, centred at x 29.0 cm and y +18.0 cm (left pier, 20 mm tall) and y -18.0 cm (right pier, 30 mm tall). (2) Datum posts: two fixed grey-painted steel posts, 20 x 20 mm and 70 mm tall with their top 10 mm painted red, centred at x 35.5 cm, y +23.0 cm and -23.0 cm (25 mm behind each pier's far face and 10 mm outboard of its outer face). Their tops, 70 mm above the table, mark the datum; their inner faces are 440 mm apart, so the beam cannot be laid across them. (3) Packers: six loose beech blocks, each 50 x 50 mm, colour-coded by thickness: yellow 20 mm (36 g), blue 30 mm (54 g), green 40 mm (72 g); a packer's two 50 x 50 mm faces are alike. Each arm has a set of three lying flat on a 50 x 50 mm face, sides parallel to x and y, in a row at y +30.0 cm (left set) or y -30.0 cm (right set): yellow centred at x 16.0 cm, blue at 22.0 cm, green at 28.0 cm (10 mm gaps). (4) Beam: a loose spruce beam, 420 mm long, 40 mm wide and 30 mm thick, 227 g, lying flat on a 420 x 40 mm face with its length along y, centred at x 15.0 cm, y 0. The left pier is 50 mm short of the datum and the right 40 mm: from one set only yellow + blue makes 50 and only green makes 40 (a yellow from each set also makes 40, but then the left cannot be packed). Laid centred across the packed piers, the beam covers each top packer from edge to edge, its ends 5 mm past their outer edges: 50 mm of bearing at each end. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged on the end state from the objects' poses (in a real trial: a straightedge from the datum post's top, a feeler gauge, a rule and a phone level). 'Still' means moved less than 3 mm and turned less than 2 degrees in the last 0.5 s. A packer is 'on' a pier when its centre, seen from above, is over the pier's 60 x 60 mm top or within 15 mm of it and its lowest point is more than 10 mm above the table. A packer on a pier 'counts' when it lies flat (its thickness axis within 3 degrees of vertical), its outline seen from above stays within the pier's top extended by 5 mm on every side, it rests on the pier's top or on a counted packer (its underside within 2 mm of that surface at its centre, its centre over that packer) and it is still. A pier is 'packed' when at least one packer is on it, every packer on it counts and the top of its highest packer is within 3 mm of the datum (70 mm above the table). The beam 'rests on' a surface when its underside is within 2 mm of it where they meet (a support up to 3 mm into it, contact penetration, still counts; anything lying on the beam is not a support). The beam is 'seated' when both piers are packed and it lies on one of its four long faces (the axis through that pair of faces within 5 degrees of vertical), is level along its length within 1.25 degrees, rests on each pier's top packer with its centre line crossing that packer and at least 30 mm of its length over it, and is still. Score 0 if any packer on a pier stands on an edge or end (its thickness axis more than 45 degrees from vertical: on the 20 mm pier any packer on edge reaches exactly 70 mm), or if the beam rests across both piers (on each it rests on the pier's top or on a packer on it) out of level by more than 1.25 degrees: a beam set on bad packing (packers come in 10 mm steps: across two tops 10 mm or more apart in height it tilts at least 1.36 degrees, across two packed piers at most 1.19). Otherwise 0.25 for each packed pier, plus 0.5 if the beam is seated. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0 (0.75 cannot occur: seating needs both piers packed). Examples: nothing packed 0; one pier packed 0.25; both packed with the beam on the table, held above them or with under 30 mm of bearing 0.5; both packed and the beam seated 1.0; the beam across a packed pier and a bare one (6 to 8 degrees) or one whose packing is 10 mm off (about 1.6 degrees) 0; the beam level on two stacks both 10 mm too high 0 (neither is packed). Packers and the beam anywhere else (on the table, on a post) are ignored; a packer lying on the beam over a pier stops that pier being packed. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 3 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. The scorer reads only the objects, not the grippers: a packer or beam still held is scored where it is.
fidelity: Rigid boxes with the simulator's default friction; the piers and posts are fixed. Real packers and shims are 1-10 mm plastic or steel plates; here they are 20-40 mm wooden blocks so a gripper can hold them, colour-coded by thickness as real packer sets are. No mortar, fixings or load test. The scorer reads only the objects' poses, so a part still held is scored where it lies.
reset_notes: Put the six packers back flat on their marks, sides parallel to x and y (each set in a row at y +30 cm or -30 cm: yellow at x 16 cm, blue at 22 cm, green at 28 cm) and the beam flat on a 420 x 40 mm face, its length along y, centred at x 15 cm, y 0. The piers and posts are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
